h: Build a medical science day across London
p: If Centre of the Cell gets your youngsters fired up about bodies and medicine, London has a handful of other places that make a brilliant follow-up. Wellcome Collection on Euston Road is a free museum and library exploring health, medicine and what it means to be human. It's thoughtful, sometimes surprising and best suited to older children, teens and adults.

Over in Lincoln's Inn Fields, the Hunterian Museum at the Royal College of Surgeons reopened in 2023 after a major refurbishment. It's home to the collection of 18th-century surgeon John Hunter, with anatomical specimens that are fascinating for budding doctors, though a bit much for the squeamish. And the Science Museum in South Kensington has its large Medicine galleries, which make a great day out on their own.

Closer to Whitechapel itself, the Whitechapel Gallery is a respected free contemporary art gallery on Whitechapel High Street, and the Young V&A in Bethnal Green is a museum of design and play aimed squarely at children and families. On a Sunday morning, Columbia Road Flower Market is a riot of colour and noise a short hop away.

A practical tip for teachers and group leaders: because sessions are booked, ask when you reserve what age range and topic the session is aimed at, so you can prepare the group beforehand. A little bit of groundwork in class means they'll get far more from the time with the scientists.
For food, the area around Whitechapel Road is famous for South Asian cooking, so nobody goes hungry.
